body.en:
Question B-007-004-008.

Why the correct answer is right: Selective fading comes from components of the same transmission arriving with phase differences at the receiver, affecting parts of the signal unequally.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Small changes in directional antenna heading at the receiving station": Small changes in directional antenna heading at the receiving station can change signal strength, but that is not the propagation cause of selective fading.
- sourceIndex 2: "Time differences between the receiving and transmitting stations": Time differences between the receiving and transmitting stations confuse clock time with path-delay phase differences.
- sourceIndex 3: "Large changes in the height of the ionosphere at the receiving station ordinarily occurring shortly before sunrise and sunset": Large changes in the height of the ionosphere at the receiving station ordinarily occurring shortly before sunrise and sunset is too specific and misses the multipath phase mechanism.
